sections.text: The king Yudhishthira, the son of Kunti, blew the Anantavijaya; Nakula and Sahadeva blew the Sughosha and the Manipushpaka.
The king of Kasi, an excellent archer, Sikhandi, the mighty car-warrior, Dhrishtadyumna and Virata and Satyaki, the unconquered.
Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, O Lord of the earth, and the son of Subhadra, the mighty-armed, blew their conches separately.

We are now discussing Chapter 1, Arjuna Vishada Yoga, the Yoga of Arjunas Grief. In the first 12 verses we have seen so far that Dhritarashtra is very anxious to know whats happening with his sons and Pandus sons. Mamakaha Pandavaschaiva, so in the very first verse we see the cause for this war. Dhritarashtra was the guardian after Pandu died for Pandus sons.
When you assign a guardian to take care of children, that guardian is responsible for their welfare and well-being and to protect their interests. Thats the job of a guardian. Dhritarashtra, being the Emperor and the uncle of Pandus sons, was assigned to take care of them.
It was Dhritarashtras duty to treat Pandus children as his own, because he was the guardian. But we clearly see how he had a distinction in his mind between his sons and Pandus sons. Mamakaha Pandavaschaiva, that is the cause for this conflict in life. We see that conflict occurs only when someone is not doing his or her duty.
Conflicts are there because someone assigned a duty is not doing it, whether it is you or the other. Therefore you also have Dharmakshetra Kurukshetra here. The goal for this war is to establish Dharma again, to re-establish Dharma.
Conflict occurs because there is a violation of Dharma somewhere. Who is responsible? One has to figure out. In the next 11 verses, we have seen whats happening with three of them.
Dhritarashtra was very anxious to know whats going on because he obviously wasnt really sure. Duryodhana, in a similar situation, has his own doubts about the loyalty of his own people and generals. He knew for sure that his cause is not validated by all the great generals in his army; he cannot feel comfortable.
They are completely loyal to him. Their loyalties may be divided. They are on my side because of their employment, that they are employed by the kingdom but their hearts may be on the other side.
It is quite well known that Arjuna was Dronas favorite student. Bheeshma liked Pandavas more than the Kauravas, so he wasnt sure. So the cause of anxiety which we see here is my own failure to follow my own Dharma.
So all these 12 verses tell us that conflict only occurs when Dharma is violated, and your peace of mind is shattered only when Dharma is violated. When you dont follow your Dharma, your mental peace will be disturbed. We see in Duryodhana that hes suffering from anxiety, and his first target was Drona, because it was quite obvious that Drona has a soft corner for Arjuna and the Pandavas.
We have seen his behavior, he enumerates who are on their side and our side, whether our army is enough or not enough. Now we are seeing Bhishma. Bhishma, being the guardian of Hastinapurs throne.
No matter what the situation, he had the duty to keep the army motivated. He realized that if he leaves this situation any longer, not only is Duryodhana going down, but hes going to bring everybody else down with him, Drona and whoever else he is addressing. So in verse 12, he said Tasya Sanjanayan Harsham, to cheer them up to fight this battle. Simhanadam vinadya ucchaih shankham dadhmau pratapavan. He roared like a lion and then blew his own conch.
So we have discussed last time the declaration of the war. Bheeshma has also come to the conclusion that this conflict can only be settled by this war. Dharma can only be established by just fighting this war.
And therefore lets get it done. So he blew his own conch. And now we see the reaction, Quick response from everybody.
As soon as Bheeshma blew his own conch, everybody else blew their own conches. There was a great sound, everybody playing their kettledrums and cow-horns. Now, there is a reason why armies used to carry those kettledrums.
We also know that sound has its own effect. When you go to a disco, the beats, as the yoga teacher will say, will activate your Muladhara chakra, they will make you dance whether you want to or not. As soon as the beat starts, you start dancing.
So the sound has its own effect in changing your mental makeup. So this great sound will put you into frenzy to do something. So that as soon as the leader has announced that we are ready, everybody else supported and said we are ready too.
We have seen the response by the army. Now here interesting thing to note is Bhagavan Vedvyas does not enumerate all the Kauravas generals who blew their conscience. But he does enumerate the Pandavas Tathahas, Swetaihi Hayehi, Yukte Mahati, Syandanesh, Titao, Madhavah, Pandavah, Chayeva, Divya, Sankam, Pradhadvatuhu.
The very first response comes from Madhav seated in the great chariot yoked by white horses. Pandav Arjun Pandus son. Pandav here is Arjun Divya, Sankhopra, Dhatma.
They believe their own divine conscience. Bhagavan Vedvyas didnt say first. Drishtadhamna did that because he was the chief of the army.
Yudhishthir not an Arjun Madhavah. The one person who was really keen in establishing Dharma in Aryavarth was Krishna. He has concluded that this conflict cannot be settled.
All the arrogance of Kauravas and their mistreatment to the people will only stop if they are stopped in their tracks. The only way to stop them is to have this war. So the first response actually came from Madhava, Krishna, who had decided hes not going to take up arms himself.
He said, Im not fighting. So sometimes without fighting directly, you can still fight the battle. The lesson to be learned here is you dont have to be always actively making noise. You can very silently win the war.
Both Madhava and Pandava Arjuna blew their own divine conches. Bhagavan Vedvyasa seems somewhat biased here. He didnt say the conches on the other side were divine, but he specifically said the Pandava conches were divine.
What this means is their cause was divine, to fight this war. Their cause was not driven by their own arrogance or self-interest. Their cause was driven by establishing Dharma. Panchajanyam Hrishikesha, Devadattam Dhananjaya, Paundram dadhmau mahasankham Bhima karma Vrikodara. Hrishikesha, Lord Krishna, blew his great Panchajanya conch.
So the conches were also named probably the sounds were unique from each other. So you can know whose conch is being blown. It is more like, you know, I dont see that now, but when we were in Africa.
So sitting in your apartment, you know whose car has come just by the noise, you know, the noise the car makes. You know, that must be Harish coming here. Oh, that sounds like Mazda.
I think that Rajan Kante from the sound of that, you can recognize who is that. So in this great war, you dont know who is where, but with your conch, you can let the other person know where you are. Your position can be determined by the sound of your conch.
Thats the way of communication. I think the yodeling in Scandinavia may be a way of communicating. So this conches were for communication.
So each one has own signature conch sound. So they know who is where in this formation of this army, how far he is from Panchajanyam. Hrishikesha, Krishnas conch was called Panchajanya because it was made from a demon called Panchajana.
There seems to be some philosophical meaning here. The conch which Krishna is blowing was born out of a demon with five attributes, the five senses. Krishna blows his own conch, working through an instrument made up of the five senses.
So its Panchajanya for Krishna. Devadattam for Arjuna, Devadatta. Indra gave him this conch, it was a gift from his father Indra.
Devadattam Dhananjaya. Paundram dadhmau mahasankham Bhima karma Vrikodara. Vrikodara means wolf-bellied, Bhima.
Because he can eat as much as he wants and still digest it like a wolf. Bhimakarma, a play on his own name, meaning the one who is capable of doing terrible deeds. He blew his own great conch named Paundra. Anantavijayam raja Kuntiputra Yudhishthira, King Yudhishthira, son of Kunti, blew his own conch called Anantavijaya, Eternal Victory. Because he is Dharmaraja, his victory is in establishing truth.
And truth has eternal victory. So therefore his conch is named Anantavijaya. Nakula Sahadeva cha Sughosha Manipushpakau, Nakula and Sahadeva also blew their conches, and they reflect their own personalities. Nakula was a fashionable one, therefore his conch is Sughosha, sweet-sounding.
Manipushpaka, decorated like a jewel, was Sahadevas. One was a fashion icon, another was an expert with horses. So their conches also reflect their personalities. Kashya cha parameshvasa, Shikhandi cha maharatha, Dhrishtadyumna, Virata cha, Satyaki cha aparajita, and all the others, such as the King of Kashi who is a great archer, Shikhandi the mighty warrior.
Shikhandi was transgender. So you can see that having transgender soldiers is not just a modern military issue. And they had the same issue whether Shikhandi can fight or not.
But Pandavas were open minded. Shikhandi never changed his gender. He was born as a girl. And Drupad raised him as a girl.
But allowed to fight in the army because they did not discriminate between who can fight in the army whether men or women. But Shikhandi, from all accepted description he changed his gender. He was born as a girl.
His mother raised her as a boy. Because Drupad wanted a son to fight Drona. But it turned out to be a girl.
So he was raised as a son. And then at some point he left his house because after he got married it created a problem. So he left and then changed his gender.
As per the Puranas, he was Amba reborn as Shikhandini. His name was Shikhandini when he was a girl, and then Shikhandi when he became a man. Also listed are Dhrishtadyumna, Drupadas other son, Virata, and Satyaki the unconquered.
Satyaki was actually from Krishnas side. Krishna gave his army to Duryodhana, but not all the generals decided to join that side. Some of them decided they wouldnt take the army but they also wouldnt fight there.
Satyaki was one of them. He decided to fight from the Pandava side. We know the story of Virata and Dhrishtadyumna.
Dhrishtadyumnas only goal in life was to kill Drona to take his fathers revenge. So you see, Shikhandis goal is to kill Bhishma, and Dhrishtadyumnas goal is to kill Drona. So they are mentioned here, just as Drona and Bhishma are on the Kaurava side, the two people who are determined to kill them are on this side. Drupada Draupadeyascha sarvashah prithivipate, Saubhadra cha mahabahu, and then all the other people, O King of the earth.
Prithivipate here is addressed to Dhritarashtra. Drupada and Draupadis sons and Saubhadra (Abhimanyu), the mighty-armed, all these great warriors blew their conches. Shankhan dadhmuh prithak prithak, they blew their own conches separately. Blowing ones own conch is like expressing ones own opinion.
Everyone has to have their own opinion. So when we are in a meeting somewhere, if you are not having a chance to have your own opinion, that meeting is worthless for you. Everyone has to express their own opinion.
Now if everybody is doing it in an orderly manner, it makes sense. But everybody is doing it at the same time. I was reading in newspaper that Mitch McConnell briefed the senators that this impeachment procedure may not be very exciting.

These verses beautifully reveal how our instruments, our conches, reflect our inner nature. Yudhishthira, the Dharmaraj, blows Anantavijaya (eternal victory), because truths victory is never temporary. Nakula blows Sughosha (sweet-sounding), reflecting his refined, aesthetic nature. Sahadeva blows Manipushpaka (jewel-bedecked), fitting his scholarly, detail-oriented character. Even the warriors instruments express who they are.
Notice also the remarkable inclusion of Shikhandi among the warriors, one who was born female as Amba, raised as male, and eventually changed gender. The Pandava army didnt discriminate about who could fight for dharma; what mattered was commitment to the cause, not conventional categories. This ancient text shows us that the battle for righteousness has always included those who dont fit neatly into societys boxes.
The verse concludes: Shankhaan dadhmuh prithak prithak, they blew their conches separately, each one expressing their individual voice. In any great endeavor, collective action requires individual commitment. Everyone must have their own conch to blow, their own opinion to voice. Reflect on where you stand in your current army. Do you have your own voice, your own clear contribution? Or are you merely following along without expressing your authentic commitment? In meetings, in relationships, in life decisions, are you blowing your own conch prithak (separately, distinctly), or have you lost your individual voice in the collective noise? The Gita suggests that true participation requires both alignment with the larger purpose and the courage to sound your unique note.
